title: Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
content:
Anthropic just announced an AI agent competitor to Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots: Claude Duet. The new agent, designed for professionals and small business owners, is launching as a “research preview,” according to Anthropic, and it’s available as a standalone app on iOS and Android and through Claude on the web.
Anthropic takes on Muse with Claude Duet, its new AI agent
Claude Duet is Anthropic’s new agent for professionals and small business owners, and it’s launching as a research preview.
The AI agent is built around Claude Opus 5.5. Here’s Anthropic’s description of what it can do:
Each morning, it sends you a short brief on the most important items across your connected apps. Throughout the day, it keeps tabs on those apps and messages you only when something needs your attention. You can also hand it tasks of all shapes—from simple administrative tasks of scheduling meetings to more complex ones, such as building dashboards with dozens of tools, creating financial or sales forecasts, prototyping, and building web apps.
Claude Duet pulls in memory, skills, and connected apps from Claude, and it has a virtual machine with a browser that it can use for completing work. Before any big step, like sending a payment or deleting something, Claude Duet messages you for approval. Given that Duet may be taking action on sensitive information, it has a new “new dedicated classifier and safety system prompt” that are “designed to reject requests to share the strictest tier of information,” such as credit card numbers.
Anthropic says Claude Duet is currently an “early version” and that it “still might misread a thread or miscalibrate what’s urgent.” It’s also not “as strong” at personal errands like booking tickets.
If you want to try Claude Duet, you can get on the waitlist, though you’ll need to be a Pro or Max subscriber in the US to use it.

report.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a research-preview AI agent for professionals and small businesses built on Claude Opus 5.5, competing with Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots.
report.background: Over the past two years the assistant market has shifted from chat interfaces toward agents that hold context, connect to other software and actually execute work. Anthropic had already been assembling the pieces: persistent memory, reusable skills, connectors built on its Model Context Protocol, and computer-use capabilities that let a model drive a browser inside a sandbox. Claude Duet packages those into a single product aimed at a specific buyer — professionals and small business owners who need scheduling, monitoring and reporting handled without a large ops team. The launch is also a direct competitive answer to Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, which have staked out similar prosumer territory. Notably, Anthropic is shipping Duet as a research preview with an explicit waitlist and a US-only, paid-tier restriction, a pattern that lets it gather real-world failure data on long-running autonomous tasks before committing to general availability.
key_points: Duet is a standalone product, not a chat mode: it ships as iOS and Android apps plus a web experience inside Claude, and access is limited to a waitlist for Pro and Max subscribers in the US during the research preview.

The core loop is proactive rather than reactive. It sends a morning brief summarizing important items across connected apps, then monitors those apps quietly and pings you only when something genuinely needs attention.

Task scope runs from administrative to technical: scheduling meetings, building dashboards across dozens of tools, producing financial or sales forecasts, prototyping, and building web apps. It works inside a virtual machine with a browser.

It inherits continuity from Claude — memory, skills and connected apps carry over — so it starts with accumulated context instead of a blank slate, which is the main practical advantage over bolting an agent onto a new app.

Safety is handled with approval gates plus a dedicated classifier and system prompt. Duet asks before consequential actions like sending a payment or deleting data, and is designed to refuse requests to surface the strictest tier of information such as credit card numbers.

Anthropic is unusually candid about weaknesses: Duet may misread a thread or miscalibrate urgency, and is weaker at personal errands like booking tickets — signalling a deliberate focus on work rather than consumer chores.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Duet confirms that the competitive frontier is no longer model quality but product surface: memory, connectors, permission design and trust. Anthropic entering the prosumer agent space with a restricted preview sets expectations that cautious rollout with visible failure modes becomes the norm. For developers, the interesting signal is architectural — a VM with a browser, inherited memory and skills, and a separate safety classifier layered on top. That is a reference design for anyone building agents, and it pushes the ecosystem further toward standardized connectors and auditable action logs. For regular users, the practical change is a shift from prompting to delegating: a tool that watches your apps and asks permission before acting. The approval gates are reassuring, but the honest caveats about misread threads mean users should still treat Duet as a junior assistant whose work needs review.
report.tools: To follow this space, watch Anthropic's Model Context Protocol and Claude Agent SDK for connector and agent scaffolding. Open-source options for building similar systems include browser-use and Playwright for browser control in a sandbox, LangGraph and CrewAI for multi-step agent orchestration, and Open Interpreter for local task execution. For observability and safety evaluation, Langfuse and AgentOps help trace agent actions and catch miscalibrated urgency before users do.
